en: to nod slightly; to move slightly

examples.en: He greeted me with a slight nod.

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 손가락 하나 까딱하기 싫어요.
examples.en: I'm so tired I don't want to lift a finger.
One slip and I would have been late.

examples.ko: 아이가 음악에 맞춰 발을 까딱하고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is tapping a foot to the music.

examples.ko: 누가 불러도 그는 까딱하지 않고 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: No matter who called him, he sat there without budging.
One careless move and there'll be trouble, so be careful.

explain: 고개, 손가락, 발을 살짝 움직이는 모습을 말해요. '까딱하면', '까딱하다가는'은 조금만 실수하면 나쁜 일이 생길 것 같다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. 보통 '고개를 까딱하다'처럼 목적어와 같이 써요.

phrases.example: 동생은 집안일에는 손가락 하나 까딱하지 않아요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling doesn't lift a finger to do housework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금도 일을 하지 않고 가만히 있을 때 쓰는 말이에요. 게으른 사람을 비판하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone does no work at all and just stays still. It carries a tone of criticizing a lazy person.

explain_en: It describes a slight movement of the head, a finger or a foot. '까딱하면' and '까딱하다가는' are commonly used to mean that one small mistake could bring bad results. It is usually used with an object, as in '고개를 까딱하다'.

examples.ko: 아침을 안 먹었더니 배가 계속 꾸르륵거려요.
examples.en: I skipped breakfast, so my stomach keeps rumbling.

examples.ko: 속이 꾸르륵거리는 걸 보니 체한 것 같아요.
examples.en: My belly is gurgling, so I think I have indigestion.
My stomach was rumbling, so I went to the restroom.
In the quiet classroom, only my stomach rumbled.

examples.ko: 배가 꾸르륵거리면 따뜻한 물을 마셔 보세요.
examples.en: If your stomach rumbles, try drinking warm water.

examples.ko: 찬 음료를 마시자 뱃속이 꾸르륵거리기 시작했어요.
examples.en: After I drank the cold drink, my belly started to gurgle.

explain: 배고플 때뿐 아니라 소화가 잘 안 되거나 찬 걸 마셨을 때처럼 배 속에서 소리가 날 때도 써요. '배가 꾸르륵거리다' 또는 '배에서 꾸르륵 소리가 나다'로 말해요. 'ㅗ'로 '꼬르륵거리다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: My stomach keeps rumbling, so I'm embarrassed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꾸르륵거리다'와 뜻이 같고 조금 더 편한 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 꾸르륵거리다, a bit more casual.

phrases.en: I'm hungry, so my stomach is growling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅗ'로 바꾼 말로 배고플 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 'ㅗ' variant, used more often when hungry.

phrases.en: I can hear a rumbling sound from my stomach.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 배 속에서 나는 소리를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -는 it describes the sound coming from the stomach.

explain_en: It is used not only when you are hungry but any time your belly makes sounds, such as with poor digestion or after a cold drink. You can say '배가 꾸르륵거리다' or '배에서 꾸르륵 소리가 나다'. It can also be said with 'ㅗ' as '꼬르륵거리다'.

examples.en: I did not go along with my friend's opinion.

examples.ko: 다들 그 말에 동조해서 회의가 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Everyone sided with that remark, so the meeting ended quickly.
He sided with the majority's claim.

examples.ko: 아무도 그의 생각에 동조할 사람이 없어요.
examples.en: There is nobody who would side with his idea.
More people are going along with the mood.
Please don't pretend to go along with me on purpose.

explain: '동조하다'는 '의견에 동조하다'처럼 '~에' 붙여 써요. '동의하다'는 내 생각도 같다는 뜻이고, 동조하다는 다른 사람이나 분위기를 따라가는 느낌이 있어요. 말보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I went along with the mood and laughed too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각보다 주변 분위기를 따라갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you follow the surrounding mood rather than your own thought.
phrases.en_equiv: to go along with the mood

phrases.en: The number of people who agree with his claim has grown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 의견을 따르는 사람들을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe people who follow a certain opinion.

phrases.en: I do not go along with that method.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따르고 싶지 않다는 뜻을 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says you do not want to follow.

explain_en: 동조하다 takes ~에, as in 의견에 동조하다. 동의하다 means your own view is the same, while 동조하다 carries a feeling of following another person or the mood. It shows up more in writing and the news than in speech.

en: as a rule; by rights; ought to

examples.ko: 학생이라면 모름지기 공부를 열심히 해야 해요.
examples.en: A student should, above all, study hard.
A person ought to keep their promises.

examples.ko: 사람이란 모름지기 그 생각이 올발라야 한다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think that a person ought to have upright thoughts.

examples.ko: 부모는 모름지기 아이의 말을 먼저 들어 줘야 해요.
examples.en: Parents should, first of all, listen to their children.

examples.ko: 의사는 모름지기 환자를 먼저 생각해야 해요.
examples.en: A doctor must, above all, think of the patient first.

examples.ko: 친구라면 모름지기 어려울 때 도와줘야 해요.
examples.en: A friend should help when times are hard.

explain: '~라면 모름지기 ~해야 한다'처럼 당연히 지켜야 할 도리를 말할 때 써요. 뒤에 '-어야 하다', '-는 법이다' 같은 표현이 와요. 말투가 약간 훈계하는 느낌이라서 어른이 하는 말이나 글에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: If you're a student, you should do your homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 역할이나 신분을 먼저 말하고 그에 맞는 도리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Name a role or status first, then say the duty that goes with it.
phrases.en_equiv: if you are X, you ought to

phrases.example: 친구는 모름지기 어려울 때 도와야 해요.
phrases.en: A friend should help when times are hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당연히 해야 하는 일을 강하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say strongly what one should naturally do.

phrases.example: 사람은 모름지기 노력한 만큼 얻는 법이에요.
phrases.en: As a rule, people get back what they put in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세상의 이치나 원칙을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state a principle or the way things are.

explain_en: It is used to state a duty that naturally should be followed, as in '~라면 모름지기 ~해야 한다'. It is followed by expressions such as '-어야 하다' or '-는 법이다'. The tone is a bit preachy, so you often see it in what adults say and in writing.

examples.ko: 우리는 식탁에 빙 둘러앉아서 밥을 먹었어요.
examples.en: We sat all around the table and ate.
The child spun around on the spot.
The road was blocked, so I came back the long way around.

examples.ko: 호수를 빙 돌면 삼십 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: Going all the way around the lake takes about thirty minutes.
The carousel slowly goes around.
I walked around the classroom checking the homework.

explain: 원을 그리듯 한 바퀴 도는 모양을 나타내고 '빙 돌다', '빙 둘러앉다'처럼 써요. '빙글빙글'은 여러 번 계속 도는 느낌이고, 빙은 한 번 크게 도는 느낌이에요. 눈물이 고이거나 어지러울 때는 '핑'을 써요.

phrases.en: The road was blocked, so we took a roundabout way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧바로 가지 않고 둘러서 갈 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when going around instead of straight.

phrases.en: People stood in a circle around the singer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여럿이 한 사람이나 물건 둘레에 서는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes many people standing around one person or thing.

phrases.en: The top spins round and round.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빙'과 달리 여러 번 계속 도는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike '빙', it feels like turning many times continuously.

explain_en: It shows going around in a circle, as in '빙 돌다' (go around) and '빙 둘러앉다' (sit in a circle). '빙글빙글' feels like turning again and again, while 빙 is one big turn. For welling tears or dizziness, use '핑'.

en: to habituate; to make something a part of life

examples.en: The city hall is promoting making waste separation a part of daily life.
The kindergarten teaches children to make greeting a habit.

examples.ko: 건강을 위해 운동을 생활화한 사람이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More people are making exercise part of their daily routine for their health.

examples.ko: 하루 십 분 독서를 생활화하면 달라질 거예요.
examples.en: If you make ten minutes of reading a day a habit, things will change.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 물 절약을 생활화해서 수도 요금이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Our family made saving water a habit, so our water bill went down.

examples.ko: 환경 보호를 생활화하기는 말처럼 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Making environmental protection a part of daily life is not as easy as it sounds.

explain: '습관이 되다'와 비슷하지만 '생활화하다'는 일부러 노력해서 일상에서 늘 하게 만든다는 느낌이 강해요. '절약, 운동, 독서, 안전 수칙'처럼 좋은 행동에 쓰고, 캠페인이나 교육 문장에 많이 나와요. 저절로 그렇게 되는 것은 '생활화되다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The poster says, 'Let's make recycling a part of daily life.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 하자고 권할 때 쓰는 형태로 포스터나 캠페인에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A 'let's' form often seen on posters and campaigns.
phrases.en_equiv: let's make it a daily habit

phrases.example: 일찍 일어나는 습관이 이미 생활화되어 있어요.
phrases.en: Waking up early is already a part of my daily life.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생활화하다'의 피동 표현으로, 이미 일상이 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, meaning it has already become part of daily life.

phrases.example: 매일 운동하는 것이 이제 습관이 됐어요.
phrases.en: Exercising every day has now become a habit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 노력의 느낌보다 저절로 몸에 밴 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but it feels more like something that happened naturally than something done on purpose.

explain_en: It is similar to '습관이 되다', but '생활화하다' stresses deliberately working to do something every day. It is used for good behaviors such as saving, exercise, reading or safety rules, and appears in campaigns and education. When it happens by itself, you say '생활화되다'.

en: to be disappointed; to feel hurt

examples.en: I'm really hurt that you forgot our promise.
If you say it like that, I feel hurt.
I felt hurt that my friend left without any word.

examples.ko: 생일을 모른 척하면 섭해서 말도 안 나와요.
examples.en: If you pretend not to know my birthday, I'm too hurt to speak.

examples.ko: 제대로 인사도 못 드려서 섭하실 거예요.
examples.en: You'll probably feel sad that I couldn't say a proper goodbye.
Please don't take it too hard.

explain: '섭섭하다'의 줄임말이라 대화에서 더 가볍게 들려요. 기대만큼 대해 주지 않아서 서운할 때 쓰고 '서운하다'와 비슷해요. '간섭하다'의 '섭'과는 상관없어요.

phrases.en: I'm not hurt at all even if you say that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 서운하지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says you don't feel hurt.

phrases.en: I feel hurt because my friend hasn't contacted me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '섭하다'의 원래 말이고 조금 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the full form of 섭하다 and sounds a bit softer.

phrases.en: I felt hurt but didn't say anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: '섭한 + 명사'로 서운한 감정을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: '섭한 + noun' describes the feeling of being hurt.

explain_en: It is a shortened form of '섭섭하다' and sounds lighter in conversation. You use it when someone doesn't treat you as well as you expected, similar to '서운하다'. It is unrelated to the '섭' in '간섭하다'.

examples.en: The ending of that movie is really shocking.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 소식이 너무 쇼킹해서 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: The sudden news was so shocking that I couldn't speak.
A shocking photo became a hot topic online.
Isn't it shocking that that person is the boss?

examples.ko: 처음 먹어 본 음식이 쇼킹한 맛이었어요.
examples.en: The food I tried for the first time had a shocking taste.
My friends are going crazy saying the twist was shocking.

explain: '충격적이다'와 비슷하지만 '쇼킹하다'는 더 가볍고 구어적이라 친구끼리 놀랄 때 잘 어울려요. 좋은 놀라움에도 나쁜 놀라움에도 쓰지만, 진지한 뉴스나 글에서는 '충격적이다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I heard really shocking news today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 줄 때는 '쇼킹한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 쇼킹한 to modify a noun.

phrases.en: The scene I saw yesterday was so shocking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구끼리는 반말 '쇼킹했어'로 편하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Among friends, use the casual 쇼킹했어.

phrases.en: That story isn't very shocking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀랍지 않다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is not surprising.

explain_en: It is similar to '충격적이다', but '쇼킹하다' is lighter and more colloquial, fitting surprise among friends. It can be used for good or bad surprises, but in serious news or writing, '충격적이다' is used.

examples.ko: 우리 반 악동이 또 장난을 쳤어요.
examples.en: The rascal of our class played a prank again.
That child is a famous troublemaker in the neighborhood.
The rascals popped balloons and ran away.
When I was little, I was called a rascal.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 무대 위에서 악동 같은 모습을 보여요.
examples.en: That singer shows a bad-boy side on stage.
A cartoon starring a troublemaker is popular.

explain: '개구쟁이'는 귀엽게 장난치는 아이이고, '악동'은 말썽이 더 큰 느낌이에요. 가수나 운동선수의 이미지를 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: That singer is like a rascal on stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장난이 많고 거침없는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 이미지를 말할 때도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone playful and bold, often used about a public image.

phrases.en: That player is called a bad boy by fans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 별명이나 이미지를 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a nickname or image.

phrases.en: My son is a mischievous kid at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '악동'보다 귀엽고 가벼운 느낌이에요. 어린아이에게 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Cuter and lighter than '악동'. Often used for young children.

explain_en: 개구쟁이 is a kid who plays pranks in a cute way, while 악동 feels like more trouble. It is also used for the image of singers or athletes.

en: undeniably; clearly; as a plain fact

examples.en: I am, without question, the owner of this house.
There are clearly rules, so please follow them.
That is undeniably illegal.

examples.ko: 엄연히 약속한 일인데 잊으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: We definitely promised, so you can't forget it.
Even though he's young, he is very much a member of the team.

examples.ko: 엄연히 주인이 있는 물건이니까 함부로 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This item clearly has an owner, so you can't just use it freely.

explain: 누가 모르는 척하거나 무시할 때 '분명한 사실이 있다'고 강하게 말하는 부사예요. 보통 '엄연히 ~이다', '엄연히 ~가 있다'로 쓰고, '분명히'와 뜻은 비슷한데 더 단호해요. 처음에는 '분명히'를 먼저 써도 돼요.

phrases.en: I definitely put it here, but it's gone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엄연히'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 부드럽고 일상에서 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 엄연히 but softer and much more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: That is an undeniable fact.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엄연히'의 모양이 바뀐 말로, 명사 앞에서 써요. 모르는 척하는 사람에게 사실을 강하게 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form of 엄연히 used before a noun; it stresses a fact to someone who is ignoring it.

phrases.en: Even twins are clearly different people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷해 보여도 분명히 다르다고 단호하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to firmly say two things are plainly different even if they look alike.

explain_en: This adverb is used when someone ignores or pretends not to know a fact, to say firmly that it clearly exists. It usually appears as '엄연히 ~이다' or '엄연히 ~가 있다', and is like '분명히' but more firm. At first it is fine to use '분명히' instead.

examples.en: Anyway, just get a good rest today.
At any rate, I will definitely be there by the appointed time.

examples.ko: 이유가 뭐든 여하간 사과부터 해야 해요.
examples.en: Whatever the reason, you should apologize first.
Anyhow, the result is good, so I'm relieved.

examples.ko: 비가 오든 안 오든 여하간 출발해요.
examples.en: Rain or shine, let's set off anyway.
Anyway, let's talk about that later.

explain: '어쨌든', '아무튼', '여하튼'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요. 일상 대화에서는 '어쨌든'이나 '아무튼'이 더 자연스럽고, '여하간'은 조금 딱딱하게 들려요. 이야기를 정리하거나 화제를 돌릴 때 문장 앞에 와요.

phrases.en: Anyway, I'm glad we arrived on time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여하간'과 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and more natural in everyday talk.

phrases.en: Anyhow, health is the most important thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기를 정리하며 핵심을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to wrap up and state the main point.

phrases.en: At any rate, I'll let you know when the results come out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여하간'과 거의 같고, 조금 딱딱한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 여하간, with a slightly stiff tone.

explain_en: It means the same as '어쨌든', '아무튼', and '여하튼'. In daily talk '어쨌든' or '아무튼' sounds more natural, and '여하간' is a bit stiff. It comes at the start of a sentence to wrap up or change the topic.

examples.en: I feel chilly, maybe because I'm coming down with a cold.
I got rained on, and my body is shivering with chills.
I felt a chill, so I pulled the blanket over me.
I've had chills since this morning. Should I go to the doctor?
When evening came, I got chills and goosebumps.
Warm ginger tea is good when you have the chills.

explain: 열이 나려고 하거나 비를 맞은 뒤처럼 몸이 오싹오싹 추운 느낌에 써요. 날씨 자체보다 몸 상태 때문에 한기가 들 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Since this morning my body has been feeling chilly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으슬으슬' 뒤에 '하다'를 붙여 상태를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 turns it into a verb describing a state.

phrases.en: When evening came, I started to feel a chill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 차고 오싹해지는 느낌을 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for the cold, shivery feeling in the body.

phrases.example: 비 맞고 와서 으슬으슬 춥고 열도 나요.
phrases.en: I came back after getting rained on, and I feel chilly and have a fever too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감기 기운이 있을 때 몸이 추운 느낌에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the cold feeling in the body when you're coming down with a cold.

explain_en: It describes shivery chills in the body, like when a fever is coming on or after getting rained on. It fits best when the chill comes from your body's condition rather than just the weather.

examples.ko: 해 보기도 전에 지레 포기하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't give up in advance before you even try.

examples.ko: 아직 모르는데 지레 겁먹을 필요 없어요.
examples.en: You don't know yet, so there's no need to get scared ahead of time.

examples.ko: 아이가 혼날까 봐 지레 울음을 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: The child burst into tears before even being scolded, fearing it would happen.
I got disappointed before the results even came out.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 거절할 거라고 지레 생각했어요.
examples.en: I assumed in advance that he would refuse.
I worried in advance and couldn't sleep.

explain: 일이 일어나기도 전에 먼저 앞서서 한다는 뜻이라서 걱정, 포기, 겁먹다, 짐작하다 같은 말과 자주 써요. '미리'는 보통 중립적이지만 '지레'는 필요 이상으로 앞서간다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 아직 시작도 안 했는데 왜 지레 겁먹어요?
phrases.en: You haven't even started yet, so why are you getting scared in advance?
phrases.nuance_ko: '지레'가 붙으면 일이 일어나기도 전에 필요 없이 먼저 무서워한다는 느낌이 생겨요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '지레' gives the sense of getting scared too early, before anything has happened.

phrases.en: It seemed hard, so I gave up before even trying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해 보지도 않고 먼저 그만둔다는 아쉬운 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It carries a regretful sense of quitting without even trying.

phrases.example: 일어나지도 않은 일을 지레 걱정하지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't worry in advance about things that haven't happened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그냥 '걱정하다'와 달리 아직 오지 않은 일을 앞서 걱정한다는 뜻이 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike plain '걱정하다', it clearly means worrying about something that hasn't happened yet.

explain_en: It means doing something ahead of time before the thing has even happened, so it often goes with worry, giving up, getting scared and guessing. '미리' is usually neutral, but '지레' feels like jumping ahead more than necessary.

examples.ko: 간호사가 다친 곳을 빠르게 처치해 줬어요.
examples.en: The nurse quickly treated the injury.
In the emergency room, the doctor treats the patient first.
I don't know how to deal with this problem.

examples.ko: 상처를 잘못 처치하면 더 심해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you treat a wound wrong, it can get worse.

examples.ko: 집 안에 쌓인 잡동사니를 한꺼번에 처치하느라 힘들었어요.
examples.en: It was hard getting rid of all the clutter piled up in the house at once.

examples.ko: 산에서 다쳤을 때 처치하는 방법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned how to treat an injury when you get hurt in the mountains.

explain: 의사나 간호사가 다친 곳이나 병을 다룰 때 써요. 일상에서는 '응급 처치'라는 말로 더 자주 듣고, 가벼운 상처는 '치료하다'를 써요. 골칫거리를 치우거나 없앨 때도 쓰는데, 치우기 어려운 물건을 보면 '처치 곤란'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 넘어진 아이에게 응급 처치를 해 줬어요.
phrases.en: I gave first aid to the child who fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급한 상황에서 먼저 하는 처치를 말할 때 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for the first care given in an urgent situation.

phrases.en: I received quick treatment at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when speaking from the patient's point of view.

phrases.en: The doctor treated my wound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가벼운 상처나 병에는 '치료하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For minor wounds or illness, 치료하다 sounds more natural.

explain_en: Doctors and nurses use it for dealing with an injury or illness. In daily life you mostly hear '응급 처치' (first aid), and for a small wound people say '치료하다'. It can also mean getting rid of a nuisance; '처치 곤란' describes something hard to get rid of.

dis.h: give quick first-aid care on the spot

p.n: 처치하다 is immediate care; 치료하다 is the whole treatment.

examples.en: I was thirsty, so I moistened my lips with water.

examples.ko: 마른 목을 축이려고 시원한 차를 마셨어요.
examples.en: I drank some cold tea to wet my dry throat.

examples.ko: 화분 흙이 말랐으니 물로 축여 주세요.
examples.en: The soil in the pot is dry, so please moisten it with water.

examples.ko: 마라톤 도중에 물 한 모금으로 목을 축이기도 해요.
examples.en: During a marathon, people sometimes wet their throat with a sip of water.

examples.ko: 걸레를 물에 축이고 짜서 바닥을 닦았어요.
examples.en: I dampened the rag in water, wrung it out, and wiped the floor.
Shall we take a short break and wet our throats with coffee?

explain: '적시다'보다 물기를 조금 묻혀 촉촉하게 하는 느낌이고, '목을 축이다', '입술을 축이다'가 대표적이에요. 발음은 [추기다]이고, 마르지 않고 습한 느낌의 '축축하다'와 한 계열의 말이에요.

phrases.en: Let's sit down for a moment and have a drink before we go.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목을 적신다는 말이지만 실제로는 물이나 차를 가볍게 마신다는 뜻이에요. 많이 마시기보다 목마름을 잠깐 달랠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Literally it means wetting your throat, but in practice it means having a light drink of water or tea. It suggests a quick sip to ease thirst rather than drinking a lot.

explain_en: Compared with '적시다' (to soak), it feels like adding a little moisture, and '목을 축이다' and '입술을 축이다' are the typical uses. It is pronounced [추기다], and it belongs to the same family as '축축하다' (damp).

examples.en: When a child does something wrong, I discipline them calmly.
I learned how a teacher disciplines students.

examples.ko: 동생이 거짓말을 해서 부모님이 차분하게 훈육하셨어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling lied, so our parents calmly disciplined him.

examples.ko: 큰 소리 없이도 아이를 훈육할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can discipline a child even without raising your voice.

examples.ko: 어제는 아들을 너무 심하게 훈육한 것 같아 미안했어요.
examples.en: I felt sorry because I thought I had disciplined my son too harshly yesterday.

examples.ko: 일관되게 훈육하면 아이도 규칙을 잘 따라요.
examples.en: If you discipline consistently, children follow the rules well too.

explain: '가르치다'보다 잘못된 행동을 고쳐 주고 예절을 익히게 한다는 느낌이 강해요. 주로 부모나 선생님이 아이를 대상으로 하고, 보통 '아이를 훈육하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요. 말할 때는 '혼내다'보다 차분하고 교육적인 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I discipline my child calmly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훈육의 태도를 말할 때 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing for describing the manner of discipline.

phrases.en: I read about how to discipline a child in a book.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는' 모양으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the modifier form -는 to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.en: My child lied, so I scolded them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '훈육하다'보다 말투가 일상적이고 화난 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More casual and angrier in tone than 훈육하다.

explain_en: It feels stronger than '가르치다' (to teach) in the sense of correcting bad behavior and building manners. It is mostly done by parents or teachers to children and is used with an object, as in '아이를 훈육하다'. It sounds calmer and more educational than '혼내다'.
